title: Vexa channel revocation list
description: The channel's recall notice. We can publish and we cannot un-publish: an immutable tag stays resolvable and a cached chart stays installable, so withdrawing a release has to be a POSITIVE, signed statement rather than a deletion. One list per channel, cosign-signed with the same channel key that signs entries, published at <channel-ref>/revocations:latest and replaced wholesale on every revocation. ABSENT IS NOT AN ERROR: a channel that predates this capability has no list, and a verifier treats that as an empty list — stated here so nobody implements the fail-closed reading, which would brick every install made before the list existed. The list carries its own `expires` for the same reason entries do: a verifier that can reach the channel but keeps getting a months-old list is being fed a stale answer, and freshness is the only defence against that. NOT READABLE BY KYVERNO — admission controllers verify signatures on images, they do not fetch vendor documents; the PreSync verifier is the enforcement point.

channel.description: The channel this list governs. A verifier refuses a list naming a channel other than the one it pulled from.

expires.description: After this instant the list itself is stale and the verifier says so rather than trusting it. Re-published on every revocation and by `revoke --refresh` in between.

entries.description: Every withdrawal ever made on this channel, oldest first. Never pruned: a list that forgets is a list that re-admits.

digest.description: An exact artifact or image digest. The precise form: it survives re-tagging and names one immutable set of bytes.

version.description: A release version, withdrawing every entry that names it. The blunt form, for when the defect is in the release rather than in one artifact.

reason.description: Why it was withdrawn, in words an operator can act on. Not optional and not a code: this text is what a customer reads at the moment their sync stops.

severity.description: low/medium withdraw the release from new installs; high/critical mean a running install should be moved off it. The verifier refuses regardless of severity — the field tells the operator how fast to act, it does not soften the refusal.

supersedes.description: The release an operator should move to instead, when one exists. Null when the answer is 'no version yet'.

advisory.description: Link to the fuller writeup — a CVE, an advisory, a receipt in this repository.
